cells.tense: There is a direction you are walking, and you are walking it from vision rather than argument.
cells.ask: Finish one thing this week and hand it over. Then leave it finished, without reopening it to check.
cells.core:
There is a direction you are moving in. It didn't come from a spreadsheet or an argument you won; it came from a pull you could feel, and you've been following it. What you've been making has come far enough to stand on its own, and releasing it can read as a loss some days.

This is the steady face of direction. Not forcing it and not letting it drift — the way you hold something heavy for someone without crushing it. Finish one thing this week and hand it over. Then leave it finished, without reopening it to check. The next direction can sit until this one has left your hands.
cells.sheetLine: You picked a direction from vision. Keep walking it and let the work leave.
cells.verb: Choosing which direction to follow from vision rather than argument
cells.place: At the point where what has been made is finished enough to leave your hands

cells.tense: You are bracing at a future you cannot write in yet, and the bracing keeps pulling you off the direction you chose.
cells.ask: Ask one question you genuinely do not know the answer to, and let it stay unanswered for a day.
cells.core:
You are holding the direction too tightly for the stage it's in. It has become something to defend rather than follow, and talks around it turn into attempts to secure an outcome before it arrives. The pull you started from is still there, but you're facing the destination instead of the road.

This isn't a failure of direction; it's direction in excess. Trying to read the whole route from here is draining the thing that made the choice clear in the first place. Ask one question you genuinely do not know the answer to, and let it stay unanswered for a day. The choice holds even when you aren't gripping it, and not-knowing is part of how it lands.
cells.sheetLine: You already chose. Gripping the destination is costing you the road.

cells.tense: You set a direction in front of you once and you have been standing at that door long after it closed.
cells.ask: Pick the smallest piece of the old direction and do one concrete thing with it today. One step, then stop.
cells.core:
Steering isn't happening right now. A direction was chosen once, in a room behind you, and the pull has been visible but not followed; the work sits unfinished because finishing it would mean walking toward something. Staying at that door can feel like caution. It can also feel like waiting.

The direction itself hasn't gone anywhere. You are the one who hasn't moved. Insight isn't the shortage here; one small act of tending is, the kind you'd give a growing thing without exhausting yourself. Pick the smallest piece of the old direction and do one concrete thing with it today. One step, then stop. The pull is still where it was, asking you forward.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is still there. You are the one who hasn't moved.

cells.tense: You are already steering by something — it shapes what you say yes to — and you describe it as if it were arriving on its own.
cells.ask: Say out loud 'I chose this' about one thing you have been calling the work's natural direction.
cells.core:
You are already pointing somewhere. People can feel it in what you accept, what you drop, what you let matter; it comes through in the way you hold a day together. But you narrate it as if the work decided for itself, and the one person doing the work of choosing sits quietly in the middle of it, getting no credit.

The direction is running. What hasn't caught up is the saying-so. That isn't a hole in your grasp of things; it's a choice filed under something else. Say out loud 'I chose this' about one thing you have been calling the work's natural direction. The light wasn't only out there. You picked it, and the picking belongs to you.
cells.sheetLine: You already chose this. Say so, and keep the choice.

attempts.check: The one unsupported claim in the draft: that these cells can name what the person's internal state actually is, when the record only gives a capacity in a moment they could recognise. The reader could reasonably say 'nothing is broken, this is just how I work' — so the cells must narrow to the mechanism, not the history or the motive. The ask survives being wrong because it is one plain act with a finish, doable today without spare money, energy, a safe person on hand or free time; it does not depend on the read landing. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person: any line that praises the invented method — cut every one, and let the ask stand on what it actually offers.
